title: Quality Assurance in Orthognathic Surgery: Application of Experimental 3D Imaging Systems in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
summary: Precise measurement of facial shape is important for planning surgery in the facial region. Until now, specialized 3D camera systems have been used for this purpose. New technologies such as standard smartphones and so-called XR headsets (mixed-reality glasses) could make this measurement simpler and more cost-effective in the future. This study investigates how accurately a smartphone (iPhone 17 Pro) and an XR headset (Varjo XR-4 Focal Edition) can capture the face three-dimensionally. For this purpose, facial images are taken from 30 to 40 healthy volunteers using three different systems: an established 3D camera system (Vectra M3), a smartphone, and an XR headset. At 20 defined points on the face, distances are determined both manually (using a caliper) and based on the digital 3D models. The results from all methods are then compared with one another to determine how accurate the new, more cost-effective methods are compared to the established manual measurement and the conventional 3D camera system. The aim is to establish a scientific basis for whether smartphones and XR headsets can be used for 3D facial measurement in facial surgery in the future.
conditions: Anthropometric measurements are performed on healthy volunteers. Digital anthropometric methods serve as a supplementary tool in both preoperative planning and postoperative outcome evaluation in oral and maxillofacial surgery.

interventions.name: A total of 30 to 40 healthy volunteers will be examined. An iPhone 17 Pro (Apple Inc., USA) and the 3D surface scanning system Vectra M3 (Canfield Scientific, USA) are used to create the 3D surface models. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy students enrolled at LMU.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals with a recent history of craniofacial surgery, maxillofacial trauma, or significant skeletal deformities, as well as individuals with known allergies to the marker used to mark the anthropometric landmarks.
